blocks.text: 1. Context Filtering
https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785447580278-488399090.png
Context Filtering, covering how irrelevant content gets removed before it ever reaches the prompt, adds one more quality check before assembly.
It drops retrieved chunks that fail a final relevance check, even after re-ranking.
2. One More Check After Re-Ranking
Re-ranking already ordered chunks by relevance; top-K selection already limited how many pass through.
Context filtering adds one more check specifically focused on relevance quality, not just count.

blocks.content: {"headers":["Stage","Focus"],"rows":[["Re-ranking and top-K selection","Ordering and limiting how many chunks pass through"],["Context filtering","Checking whether each surviving chunk deserves to stay"]]}

blocks.text: 3. A Threshold On Genuine Relevance
https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785447580584-394176106.png
As with dynamic K selection strategies in Top-K Selection, a minimum relevance score can filter out chunks regardless of how many slots remain.
Even a top ranked chunk gets dropped if its score falls below that threshold.
4. Filtering By Metadata Constraints
https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785447580584-223935858.png
As with structure as a signal in Metadata Retrieval, a chunk's metadata can disqualify it even if its content scores well.
An outdated document or a wrong access permission both justify exclusion.

blocks.title: Note
blocks.content: A chunk from a document marked as deprecated can score very well on content relevance while still deserving exclusion, since its metadata signals it should no longer be surfaced.

blocks.text: 5. Filtering Out Low Quality Sources
https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785447580585-258376852.png
Some sources are known to be less reliable or less authoritative than others.
A filtering rule can deprioritize or exclude chunks from those weaker sources.
6. Balancing Filtering Strictness Against Recall
https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785447580585-496880533.png
As with the risk that too small a K truncates useful context in Top-K Selection, overly strict filtering can remove chunks that were actually needed.
The same tension between precision and completeness reappears here.

blocks.title: Note
blocks.content: A filtering threshold set too aggressively can strip away a chunk that, while scoring only moderately on relevance, actually contained the specific detail the query needed.

blocks.text: 7. Filtering As The Last Step Before Assembly
As with every part of the prompt takes space in Token Budgeting, filtering happens right before the surviving chunks get assembled into the final prompt.
Only chunks that pass every prior check ever reach that assembly step.
8. Combining Filtering With Compression
https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785447580585-481125984.png
Filtering removes whole chunks, while compression shrinks the chunks that remain.
Both techniques work together toward the same lean, relevant final context.

blocks.content: {"headers":["Technique","What it does"],"rows":[["Context filtering","Removes whole chunks that fail relevance or quality checks"],["Context compression","Shrinks the content of chunks that remain"]]}

blocks.text: 9. Recognizing When Context Filtering Deserves A Dedicated Pass

blocks.alt: Recognizing When Context Filtering Deserves A Dedicated Pass
blocks.text: https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785447580586-319117228.png
Collections with mixed quality or access controlled sources need context filtering.
Small, uniformly trustworthy collections may not need an additional filtering pass.
10. Worked Example
The example below directly demonstrates filtering re-ranked chunks by both a relevance threshold and metadata constraints.

code.content:
reranked_chunks = [
    {"id": "c1", "score": 0.91, "status": "current"},
    {"id": "c2", "score": 0.87, "status": "deprecated"},
    {"id": "c3", "score": 0.42, "status": "current"},
    {"id": "c4", "score": 0.78, "status": "current"},
]

def filter_by_relevance_threshold(chunks, threshold=0.6):
    # a threshold on genuine relevance
    return [c for c in chunks if c["score"] >= threshold]

def filter_by_metadata(chunks):
    # filtering by metadata constraints
    return [c for c in chunks if c["status"] == "current"]

after_relevance_filter = filter_by_relevance_threshold(reranked_chunks)
print(f"After relevance threshold filter: {after_relevance_filter}")

after_metadata_filter = filter_by_metadata(after_relevance_filter)
print(f"After metadata filter (filtering by metadata constraints): {after_metadata_filter}")

print(f"\nStarted with {len(reranked_chunks)} chunks, ended with {len(after_metadata_filter)} after both filters,")
print("filtering as the last step before assembly.")

blocks.title: Note
blocks.content: Running this example shows a low scoring chunk removed by the relevance threshold and a deprecated chunk removed by the metadata filter, exactly the combined filtering approach.

blocks.text: 11. Common Mistakes

items: Skipping a relevance threshold, letting weak matches through simply because a slot was available.
Ignoring metadata constraints like source status or access permissions during filtering.
Setting a filtering threshold so strict that needed chunks get removed.
Never combining filtering with compression, missing the full benefit of both techniques together.

blocks.text: 12. Key Takeaways

items: Context filtering drops retrieved chunks that fail a final relevance check, even after re-ranking.
It adds a check focused on relevance quality, distinct from re-ranking's ordering and top-K's count.
A minimum relevance score can filter out chunks regardless of how many slots remain available.
A chunk's metadata can disqualify it even when its content score looks strong.
Filtering rules can deprioritize or exclude chunks from known low quality or unreliable sources.
Overly strict filtering can remove chunks that were actually needed, echoing the precision versus recall tension.
Filtering happens right before surviving chunks get assembled into the final prompt.
Filtering removes whole chunks; compression shrinks what remains, working together toward a lean context.
